mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected future equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-week simple moving average
failure_condition: Over 60-day rolling window, 20-day forward returns remain non-negative despite persistent rate hikes, or the 5-week SMA reverts before the forward return materializes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in UNRATE above 5.5% for three consecutive months is associated with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as higher labor-market rigidity reduces consumer spending and corporate investment.
failure_condition: In a 200-day rolling window, the 60-day forward return is positive whenever the trigger occurs, or the effect persists only in low-inflation regimes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both HOUST (industrial production) and PAYEMS (employment) by at least 2% in the same month predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand suppresses corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous and PAYEMS < previous by ≥2%
failure_condition: Over 100 triggered events, the 20-day forward return is non-negative more than 50% of the time, or the interaction is dominated by a single variable.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in INDPRO (industrial production) below its 12-month moving average, followed by a recovery above it, coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as the signal of improving supply conditions boosts investor optimism.
failure_condition: Across 500 such triggers, the 20-day forward return is negative in more than 70% of cases, or the effect is not statistically significant after controlling for inflation and interest rates.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below its 10-year average for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 exhibits a positive 60-day forward return as lower policy rates incentivize risk-taking and equity valuation expansion.
failure_condition: In regimes with high inflation or financial stress, the 60-day forward return is not materially higher than the 10-year average baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in PAYEMS above the 12-month moving average accompanied by a decline in UNRATE below 5% predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as labor market expansion supports consumer demand and corporate hiring.
failure_condition: The interaction is not statistically significant in tight labor markets, or the forward return is negative when the trigger occurs in high-inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 3% predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as weak demand signals impending earnings weakness.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous and RSAFS < previous by ≥3%
failure_condition: Over 200 such events, the 5-day forward return is non-negative in more than 60% of cases, or the proxies are not jointly significant in regression models.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in CPIAUCSL (CPI) above the 6-month moving average in a deflationary regime predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as higher inflation erodes real earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 6-month SMA and inflation regime detected (CPIAUCSL < 3% previous month)
failure_condition: In non-deflationary regimes, the 20-day forward return is not significantly different from baseline when the trigger occurs.
